sims.title: Cavity wall explorer
sims.summary: Explore a part-built cavity wall in 3D. Build it in the right order, place the wall ties, see how water is kept out in cross-section, and spot six construction faults.
sims.instructions:
Open the link and work through the 3D cavity wall simulation (20–30 minutes). Use headphones and press Sound on.
1. Guided tour: watch all 9 stages.
2. Build it: assemble the wall in the right order and place the wall ties.
3. Spot the faults: find all 6 faults. For each one, write down what is wrong and what it causes.
4. Test yourself: answer the 5 questions. Use "Show me" if you get stuck.
Hand in your list of faults and your quiz score.

sims.title: Disc brakes & hydraulics
sims.summary: See inside a car's disc brake in 3D. Press the pedal and watch fluid pressure push the caliper piston and clamp the pads. Inspect each part, add worn pads or air in the fluid, and spot the fault from the pedal feel and stopping distance.
sims.spec: IMI Entry Level 3 – vehicle braking systems
sims.instructions:
Open the link and work through the 3D disc brake simulation (20–30 minutes). Use headphones and press Sound on.
1. Guided tour: follow all 9 steps.
2. Hold to brake: watch the fluid, the piston and the pads. Try slow motion.
3. Inspect: tap each part and note what it does and what to check.
4. Spot the fault: add worn pads, then air in the fluid. Describe the pedal feel and stopping distance for each.
5. Test yourself: answer the 5 questions.
Hand in your fault notes and your quiz score.

sims.title: Installing an AMD Threadripper CPU
sims.summary: Step through installing a Threadripper processor in an sTR5 socket in 3D: safe preparation, opening the force and rail frames, fitting the CPU in its carrier, torquing the screws in sequence, thermal paste and the cooler.
sims.spec: Pearson BTEC Level 3 IT, Unit 2 (check against your current spec)
sims.classroomTitle: Installing an AMD Threadripper CPU – 3D simulation
sims.instructions:
Open the link and work through the 3D CPU installation simulation (15–20 minutes). Use headphones and press Sound on.
1. Play the tour and watch all 12 steps. Use the step buttons to go back to anything you missed.
2. For each step, write down the action and the common mistake shown.
3. Note the screw torque and the order the screws are tightened in.
4. Open "What you'll learn", then press Test yourself and answer the questions.
Hand in your step-by-step notes and your quiz score.

sims.title: X-rays and CT
sims.summary: Explore a 3D X-ray room and CT scanner. See how an X-ray tube makes X-rays, why bone shows white and lungs dark (attenuation), and how CT measures from every angle to build slices into a 3D view. Read CT numbers in Hounsfield units, compare doses and see how distance and lead shielding protect staff.
sims.spec: Pearson BTEC L3 Applied Science (2016), Unit 21 Medical Physics Applications – learning aims B1/B2 and C
sims.classroomTitle: X-rays and CT – 3D simulation (Imaging and treatment, Part 1)
sims.instructions:
Open the link and work through the 3D X-rays and CT simulation (25–35 minutes). Use headphones and keep the sound on.
1. Guided tour: follow all 6 stages.
2. Stage 2: hover over or tap the tube parts and explain how X-rays are produced.
3. Stage 3: move the kV slider and describe how the X-ray image changes.
4. Stages 4–5: read the CT numbers for lung, fat, soft tissue and bone.
5. Stage 6: compare the doses and use the distance slider to explain the inverse square law.
6. Test yourself: do the matching task and the 6 questions.
Hand in your notes and your quiz score.

sims.title: Gamma imaging and PET
sims.summary: Follow a technetium-99m bone scan from injection to image: watch gamma rays leave the body, pass the lead collimator and flash in the gamma camera crystal as the image builds count by count. Find the hot spots, see what happens without the collimator, then watch positron annihilation in a PET-CT scanner. Explore half-life, doses and how patients and staff are protected.
sims.spec: Pearson BTEC L3 Applied Science (2016), Unit 21 Medical Physics Applications – learning aims B3 and C
sims.classroomTitle: Gamma imaging and PET – 3D simulation (Imaging and treatment, Part 2)
sims.instructions:
Open the link and work through the 3D gamma imaging and PET simulation (25–35 minutes). Use headphones and keep the sound on.
1. Guided tour: follow all 6 stages.
2. Stage 2: explain why technetium-99m suits a bone scan.
3. Stage 3: tap the collimator, crystal and photomultiplier tubes and describe what each does.
4. Stage 4: find the hot spots, then remove the collimator and describe what happens to the image.
5. Stage 5: explain how PET detects annihilation.
6. Decay tab: work out the activity left after 12 and 24 hours.
7. Test yourself: answer the 6 questions.
Hand in your notes and your quiz score.

sims.title: Inside the heart
sims.summary: Explore a beating 3D heart cut open down the middle. Follow blood through the atria, ventricles and valves, out to the lungs and round the body. Watch the valves open and shut through the cardiac cycle, compare the ventricle walls, see the coronary arteries and follow one blood cell all the way round.
sims.spec: Pearson BTEC L3 National Foundation Diploma in Sport (601/7220/4), Unit 1 Anatomy and Physiology, Topic D1 Structure of the cardiovascular system
sims.classroomTitle: Inside the heart – 3D simulation (Cardiovascular system, Part 1)
sims.instructions:
Open the link and work through the 3D heart (20–30 minutes). Use headphones and keep the sound on.
1. Guided tour: follow all 11 stages.
2. Stages 2–8: say which valves are open and shut at each step.
3. Stage 9: explain why the left ventricle wall is thicker than the right.
4. Turn Labels off, then tap each part and name it before the tip appears.
5. Stage 11: call out each stop before the blood cell reaches it.
6. Test yourself: answer the 5 questions.
Hand in your notes and your quiz score.

sims.title: Blood vessels and blood
sims.summary: Follow blood round a closed loop of vessels: an artery cut open to show its thick wall, arterioles that widen and narrow, capillaries where oxygen and nutrients swap for carbon dioxide and lactate, and a vein with valves and the skeletal muscle pump. Spin a blood sample, watch white cells and platelets at work, and switch between rest, exercise and a cold day to see the vascular shunt.
sims.spec: Pearson BTEC L3 National Foundation Diploma in Sport (601/7220/4), Unit 1 Anatomy and Physiology, Topic D1 Structure and D2 Function of the cardiovascular system
sims.classroomTitle: Blood vessels and blood – 3D simulation (Cardiovascular system, Part 2)
sims.instructions:
Open the link and work through the 3D blood vessels simulation (25–35 minutes). Use headphones and keep the sound on.
1. Guided tour: follow all 12 stages.
2. Stage 2: explain why an artery wall is thick and elastic.
3. Stage 4: give two features of a capillary that make exchange fast.
4. Stage 6: say which vein valve opens when the muscles squeeze.
5. Switch Body between At rest and Exercise and describe the vascular shunt.
6. Stage 11: explain how skin arterioles help on a cold day.
7. Test yourself: answer the 5 questions.
Hand in your notes and your quiz score.

sims.title: Stretcher bond
sims.summary: Meet the brick and see why walls are bonded. Build a half-brick stretcher bond wall course by course, turn a corner by swapping the quoin brick, finish a stopped end with a half bat and keep to 75 mm gauge. Switch on the straight joints check, then spot the fault in a badly bonded wall.
sims.spec: City & Guilds 6705-13 Level 1 Diploma in Bricklaying, Unit 104 Carrying out bricklaying activities
sims.classroomTitle: Stretcher bond – 3D simulation (Solid walling bonds, Part 1)
sims.instructions:
Open the link and work through the 3D stretcher bond simulation (15–20 minutes). Use headphones and keep the sound on.
1. Guided tour: follow all 8 stages.
2. Stage 2: explain what a straight joint is and why it weakens a wall.
3. Stage 5: describe the half lap in your own words.
4. Stage 6: say where the half bats go and why.
5. Stage 7: work out the height of 6 courses at 75 mm gauge.
6. Spot the fault: find the mistake and explain it.
7. Test yourself: answer the 5 questions.
Hand in your notes and your quiz score.

sims.title: English and Flemish bond
sims.summary: Step up from stretcher bond to one-brick solid walls, written for Level 1 learners. See how headers tie the wall together, where the queen closer goes next to the quoin header, and how the quarter lap keeps joints apart. Compare English and Flemish bond at the same height, look at the wall from above, then find the missing closer in a faulty wall.
sims.spec: City & Guilds 6705-23 Level 2 Diploma in Bricklaying, Unit 204 Building solid walling, isolated and attached piers (AC 3.6, 4.4)
sims.classroomTitle: English and Flemish bond – 3D simulation (Solid walling bonds, Part 2)
sims.instructions:
Open the link and work through the 3D English and Flemish bond simulation (15–20 minutes). Use headphones and keep the sound on.
1. Guided tour: follow all 8 stages.
2. Stage 3: say where the queen closer goes and why.
3. Switch the Bond menu between English and Flemish and describe the difference.
4. Plan view: explain how headers tie the wall together.
5. Spot the fault: find the mistake and explain it.
6. Test yourself: answer the 5 questions.
Hand in your notes and your quiz score.

sims.title: Suspended ground floors
sims.summary: See how a suspended ground floor is built and kept dry, written for Level 2 bricklayers. Build a timber floor stage by stage: oversite, DPC, honeycombed sleeper walls, wall plates, joists and airbricks. Watch air cross the void, switch to a beam-and-block floor, then find four faults that would cause damp and rot.
sims.spec: City & Guilds 6705-23 Level 2 Diploma in Bricklaying, Unit 202/602 Principles of building construction, information and communication (LO14, AC 14.1)
sims.classroomTitle: Suspended ground floors – 3D simulation (Inside the building, Part 2)
sims.instructions:
Open the link and work through the 3D suspended ground floors simulation (15–20 minutes). Use headphones and keep the sound on.
1. Guided tour: follow all 10 stages.
2. Stage 4: explain why sleeper walls are honeycombed.
3. Stage 5: write down the two minimum air gaps.
4. Turn on Airflow and describe how air crosses the void.
5. Switch to Beam-and-block and list what replaces the joists.
6. Spot the faults: find all four and explain each.
7. Test yourself: answer the 5 questions.
Hand in your notes and your quiz score.

sims.title: At the doctor's: present perfect and past simple
sims.summary: A speaking simulation for ESOL learners. You are the patient in a GP surgery and Dr Shah asks you six questions about your back pain. Answer by speaking, typing or using word tiles. Dr Shah checks your grammar (present perfect with for and since, ever and never, and past simple with finished times), corrects you and lets you try again. A calendar on the wall shows since and for.
sims.spec: Adult ESOL Core Curriculum, Entry 3 Speaking: Sc/E3.4a (present perfect and past simple with time markers), Sc/E3.3b
sims.classroomTitle: At the doctor's – 3D speaking simulation (present perfect and past simple)
sims.instructions:
Open the link and talk to Dr Shah, the GP, in the 3D simulation (10–15 minutes). Use headphones and keep the sound on.
1. Read the start screen and tap Start.
2. Answer all 6 questions in full sentences. Use Speak, Type or Tiles.
3. If Dr Shah corrects you, read the tip and try again.
4. Write down every answer that was not right first time, with the correct sentence.
5. Look at the calendar on the wall. Write one sentence with since and one with for.
6. Do it again without Grammar help and try to beat your score.
Hand in your corrected sentences and your score.

sims.title: At the shoe shop: listen and write it down
sims.summary: Listening practice for the Entry 3 speaking exam. You are returning some boots at Brookes, and Jenny the cashier gives you three pieces of information: names, numbers, email addresses and websites. Listen and write them down on screen or on paper. Jenny says each one once, so ask her to repeat, say it slowly or spell it, by speaking, typing or using word tiles. She checks your questions and your notes, and a checklist tracks the exam must-dos.
sims.spec: Ascentis Entry 3 Speaking and Listening, Task 2: 3.3 and 4.4. Adult ESOL Core Curriculum Lr/E3.4a, Sc/E3.3b
sims.classroomTitle: At the shoe shop, part 1 – listen and write it down (3D simulation)
sims.instructions:
Open the link and practise the information part of your speaking exam (10–15 minutes). Use headphones and keep the sound on.
1. Read the task and choose where you will write: on the screen or on paper.
2. Listen to Jenny. She says each piece of information once.
3. Ask Jenny to repeat, say it slowly or spell it. Use full questions, for example: Can you spell that, please?
4. Write down all three pieces of information.
5. Finish with all three exam checklist items ticked.
6. Print or screenshot your results and check them with a partner. Then try a new set.
